instruction: Speak in French. As you read this, simultaneously increase your speed from slow to fast and your volume from soft to very loud.
text: La voiture approchait lentement du virage, puis elle a accéléré, de plus en plus vite, jusqu'à franchir la ligne d'arrivée en tête sous les acclamations de la foule !

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio clearly and simultaneously follows the dynamic progression of both speed (slow to fast) and volume (soft to loud).

instruction_evidence.speed: The speech starts at a notably slow pace and gradually accelerates, becoming quite fast by the end.
instruction_evidence.volume: The volume begins softly and noticeably increases in projection and loudness as the audio progresses.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The voice sounds human-like and the transitions are smooth and natural.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The dynamic shifts perfectly match the semantic content of the sentence, adding a great deal of expressive energy to the delivery.

instruction: Speak in French. Read this sentence in a calm, neutral tone, but then react with sudden surprise on the last few words.
text: Je regardais par la fenêtre, observant les gens passer comme d'habitude, quand j'ai vu un éléphant sur un skateboard.

target_values.emotion: start with a neutral emotion, but sound suddenly surprised towards the end

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The speaker successfully starts with a calm, neutral tone and convincingly transitions into sudden surprise on the final phrase.

instruction_evidence.calm_neutral_start: The first half of the sentence is delivered in a relaxed, observational, and neutral tone.
instruction_evidence.sudden_surprise_end: There is a clear and sudden shift in pitch and energy on the last few words ('un éléphant sur un skateboard'), effectively conveying surprise.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The voice is smooth, human-like, and free of synthetic artifacts.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The transition in emotion is well-acted, with a very natural expression of disbelief adding to the realism.

instruction: Speak in French. Perform this line by transitioning from a questioning, uncertain tone to a resolute and confident one.
text: Peut-être que nous devrions attendre... ou peut-être pas. Non, j'en suis certain. C'est le moment de prendre ce risque et d'avancer.

target_values.tone: begin with a hesitant tone, but become more firm and confident as you speak

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio clearly executes the dynamic transition, starting with a hesitant and uncertain tone and effectively shifting to a firm, resolute, and confident delivery in the second half.

instruction_evidence.questioning_uncertain_start: The speaker begins with a softer, slower, and hesitant delivery for 'Peut-être que nous devrions attendre... ou peut-être pas.', effectively conveying uncertainty.
instruction_evidence.resolute_confident_end: At 'Non, j'en suis certain.', the vocal delivery distinctly shifts to become firmer, louder, and more assertive, maintaining this confidence until the end.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The speech sounds smooth, human-like, and free from synthetic artifacts.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The expressive variation is rich and well-shaped, perfectly supporting the intended emotional transition.

instruction: Speak in French. Perform this monologue by starting softly and increasing your volume throughout, ending in a powerful, loud voice.
text: Au début, ce n'était qu'un murmure dans le vent, une idée fragile, mais maintenant c'est un cri, une tempête, une force que rien ne pourra arrêter !

target_values.volume: begin by speaking quietly, then build up to a very loud volume by the end

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio clearly demonstrates a progressive increase in volume, starting relatively softly and building up to a loud, powerful finish, perfectly capturing the requested dynamic progression.

instruction_evidence.soft_start: The beginning of the monologue is spoken at a softer, more subdued volume.
instruction_evidence.volume_increase: There is a clear and steady crescendo throughout the delivery.
instruction_evidence.loud_ending: The final phrase is delivered with a loud, powerful, and intense voice.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The voice is smooth and human-like with no obvious synthetic artifacts.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The dramatic crescendo is executed with great emotional intensity and excellent pacing, significantly enhancing the meaning of the text.

instruction: Speak in French. Perform a transition of tone: from uncaring to pleading, and then from pleading to resigned disappointment.
text: Vous pouvez choisir n'importe laquelle des options, ça ne change rien. Mais ne voyez-vous pas que celle-ci est la seule qui peut nous sauver ? D'accord, alors. Il n'y a plus rien à dire.

target_values.tone: begin with an indifferent tone, then shift to a pleading one, and finish with a disappointed tone

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The speaker successfully executes the three requested tones, transitioning smoothly from indifferent, to pleading, and finally to resigned disappointment.

instruction_evidence.uncaring: The first sentence is delivered with a casual, indifferent pace and flat intonation.
instruction_evidence.pleading: The middle section shows an increase in pitch and urgency, effectively conveying a pleading tone.
instruction_evidence.resigned disappointment: The final sentence is spoken with a lower pitch, a slower pace, and a noticeable sigh-like cadence that clearly signals defeat and disappointment.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The voice sounds human-like with smooth, realistic transitions between the distinct emotional states.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The emotional shifts are very well-acted, with excellent use of pitch and pacing to clearly separate the three requested stages.

instruction: Speak in French. At a constant slow speed, begin speaking as if you are lost in thought, and then let a warm, happy feeling enter your voice as you continue.
text: On se demande parfois si on a fait les bons choix dans la vie... et puis on regarde ses enfants jouer et on sait que chaque moment en valait la peine.

target_values.speed: maintain a constant slow speed throughout

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio strictly maintains the requested slow, constant speed while successfully transitioning from a contemplative, thoughtful tone to a warmer, smiling delivery in the second half.

instruction_evidence.emotion_transition: The speaker clearly starts with a detached, thoughtful tone and introduces an audible smile and warmth from 'et puis' onwards.
instruction_evidence.speed: A constant, remarkably slow speed is maintained throughout the entire utterance as instructed.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The strict adherence to the slow speed constraint results in a highly disjointed, word-by-word delivery that sounds robotic and unnatural.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: While the intended emotions are audible, the excessively disjointed pacing prevents the expression from sounding rich or fully convincing.

instruction: Speak in French. Read this list starting at your normal pitch, let your pitch rise high in the middle, and then bring it back down to normal for the end.
text: Pour ce projet, nous aurons besoin de plusieurs choses : du papier, des ciseaux, de la colle forte, des marqueurs de toutes les couleurs, et enfin, un peu de patience.

target_values.pitch: start with a normal pitch, raise it to high in the middle, and then return to a normal pitch at the end

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio clearly follows the dynamic pitch instruction. It starts at a normal pitch, progressively raises the pitch during the list items in the middle, and returns to a normal pitch for the final phrase.

instruction_evidence.normal_start: The beginning phrase 'Pour ce projet...' is spoken at a normal, baseline pitch.
instruction_evidence.high_middle: The pitch noticeably rises during the list items ('du papier, des ciseaux...') and stays high through 'toutes les couleurs'.
instruction_evidence.normal_end: The pitch drops back down to the initial normal level for the final phrase 'et enfin, un peu de patience'.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The voice sounds human-like and the transitions between pitch levels are smooth without synthetic artifacts.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The pitch contour is naturally integrated into the flow of reading a list, making it sound expressive rather than purely mechanical.

instruction: Speak in French. Begin at a moderate speaking rate, then continuously accelerate your pace throughout the sentence.
text: Pour comprendre l'histoire de l'art moderne, il faut d'abord examiner les mouvements artistiques du dix-neuvième siècle qui ont ouvert la voie à de nouvelles formes d'expression.

target_values.speed: start at a normal pace and gradually accelerate to a fast speed

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio begins at a moderate pace and speeds up after the first phrase, but the change is binary rather than a continuous acceleration throughout the sentence.

instruction_evidence.speed: Starts moderate, then abruptly changes to a fast pace for the rest of the sentence without continuous gradual acceleration.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: Not evaluated due to instruction-following level.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: Not evaluated due to instruction-following level.

instruction: Speak in French. Deliver this line with two opposing dynamic changes: your pitch should go up, and your volume should go down.
text: C'était comme un cri puissant qui s'est transformé en un murmure strident, s'étirant vers le silence tout en devenant plus perçant.

target_values.pitch: gradually rise from low to high
target_values.volume: simultaneously fade from loud to quiet

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The delivery is largely flat and monotone, failing to execute the requested opposing dynamic changes.

instruction_evidence.pitch: The pitch remains relatively constant throughout the audio instead of gradually rising from low to high.
instruction_evidence.volume: The volume stays at a consistent level and does not fade from loud to quiet as requested.

instruction: Speak in French. Your performance should move from thoughtful (slow, normal pitch) to worried (faster, higher pitch), and finally to fearful (very fast, high pitch).
text: Je ne retrouve plus mon portefeuille, je l'avais il y a une minute... J'espère vraiment que je ne l'ai pas perdu dans la rue... Mon Dieu, mon passeport était dedans !

target_values.progression: Start thoughtful (slow, normal pitch), then become worried (faster, higher pitch), and end fearful (very fast, high pitch).

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio clearly executes the requested three-stage progression, with noticeable increases in pitch, speed, and emotional intensity at each step.

instruction_evidence.thoughtful_to_worried: The first sentence is delivered at a normal pitch and moderate pace, while the second sentence noticeably shifts to a higher pitch and faster, more worried tone.
instruction_evidence.worried_to_fearful: The final exclamation ('Mon Dieu...') reaches the highest pitch and most urgent pacing, successfully completing the three-stage dynamic progression.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The voice sounds human-like, with natural French pronunciation and no obvious synthetic artifacts.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The emotional escalation is well-acted, effectively conveying the growing panic and nicely matching the context of the text.

instruction: Speak in French. Deliver the first part with a detached, sarcastic tone. Then, let that sarcasm give way to real anger, making your voice firm and direct.
text: Ah, te voilà avec la réponse à tout. Je devrais peut-être prendre des notes pour la prochaine fois. Mais tu sais quoi ? J'en ai marre de ce petit jeu ! Ce n'est pas drôle, et les conséquences sont réelles. Il est temps que tu ouvres les yeux !

target_values.progression: Start with a sarcastic tone while emotionally neutral. Then, transition into genuine anger with a firm tone.

lalm_eval.brief_reason: The audio clearly demonstrates the requested dynamic progression. It begins with a detached, mocking tone that perfectly captures sarcasm, and effectively transitions into a louder, firmer delivery that conveys genuine anger.

instruction_evidence.stage_1_sarcastic: The first two sentences are delivered with a mockingly sweet, detached tone that sounds highly sarcastic.
instruction_evidence.stage_2_anger: From 'Mais tu sais quoi ?' onwards, the volume increases and the delivery becomes tense, firm, and genuinely angry.

bonus_evidence.naturalness: The speech is smooth, human-like, and lacks any obvious synthetic artifacts, even during the emotional escalation.
bonus_evidence.expressiveness: The delivery exhibits strong expressive variation, with excellent emotional shaping that brings out a stark contrast between the two requested emotional states.
